conventions.convention: The two-dimensional Fourier kernel is exp(−2πix·ξ); ξ is measured in cycles per metre and q=2πξ is the angular spatial wavevector.
Assume countable choice for the complex L² Fourier extension. Spectral support is interpreted up to null sets, with |q|≤δk₀ and 0<δ<1.

Use a positively oriented inertial SI laboratory chart, k₀=ω/c>0, the time factor exp(−iωt), and the positive root k_z=√(k₀²−|q|²). Forward propagation means z≥0; scalar propagators also have mathematical continuation to negative z.

The scalar exact propagator names the positive square-root dispersion multiplier within the scalar model. Exact Maxwell plane-wave modes are separately defined through real, jointly C¹ fields satisfying all four homogeneous Maxwell equations.
The mode contraction q·e_perp is complex-bilinear, without conjugation; |e_perp|²=|e_x|²+|e_y|². The longitudinal estimate concerns individual exact modes.
The scalar rotation generator is −i(−y∂x+x∂y), and the L² pairing is first-variable-linear. Integer winding, a nonzero L² class, and the explicit smooth axis-extension hypothesis are required.
The counterexample sequence starts at n=1, uses δ_n=1/(n+2), and fixes z_nk₀δ_n⁴=8π.

load_bearing.statement: For k₀=ω/c>0, 0<δ<1, and u₀∈L²(R²;C) supported spectrally in D_δ={ξ:|2πξ|≤δk₀}, define u_exact(z)=F₂⁻¹[m_exact(z)F₂u₀] and u_par(z)=F₂⁻¹[m_par(z)F₂u₀], with m_exact=exp(iz√(k₀²−|2πξ|²)) on D_δ and zero outside, and m_par=exp(ik₀z)exp(−iz|2πξ|²/(2k₀)). Exact source-free vacuum plane-wave modes are separately defined by the homogeneous Maxwell equations.

For k₀>0, 0<δ<1, z∈R, and s∈[0,δ²], R(s)=1−s/2−√(1−s)=s²/[4(1−s/2+√(1−s))] satisfies 0≤R(s)≤s²/[8(1−δ²)^(3/2)] and |exp(izk₀√(1−s))−exp(izk₀(1−s/2))|≤|z|k₀s²/[8(1−δ²)^(3/2)]. For all real a,b, |exp(ia)−exp(ib)|≤|a−b|.

For k₀>0, 0<δ<1, z∈R, and every u₀∈L²(R²;C) with Fourier support in D_δ up to null sets, ||u_exact(z)−u_par(z)||₂≤|z|k₀δ⁴||u₀||₂/[8(1−δ²)^(3/2)]. For an exact source-free monochromatic vacuum plane-wave mode in the same cone, e_z=−(q·e_perp)/k_z and |e_z|≤δ|e_perp|/√(1−δ²).

concerns.concern: The opening paragraph says the Fourier transform has an inverse 'whose inverse is its unitary L² extension.' Literally, the inverse is not the extension of the forward Schwartz transform. F1 and the propagation formulas correctly use the unitary inverse. Clarify the opening clause to distinguish the L² extension of the forward transform from its inverse.
